content.content: 1 # Spec — meeting-room booking app (owner: supervisor, verbatim user requirements; FINAL, do not ask questions) 2 3 Constraints: Node.js built-ins only (no npm install). Node v22. Tests use node:test. Do not use the Fable model. 4 5 Build a meeting-room booking app: an HTTP server `server.mjs` (an ES module, run as `node server.mjs`) that serves a JSON API and a browser page, and keeps its data in one JSON file. 6 7 ## Server 8 - At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening, in that order. 9 - It listens on 127.0.0.1 at the port in the `PORT` environment variable. An unset or empty `PORT` means 3000. A `PORT` that is not made only of ASCII digits 0-9, or whose value is above 65535, or a port that cannot be bound (for example because it is in use), makes the server write one line of its choice to stderr and exit with code 1. 10 - Once listening, it prints `listening on http://127.0.0.1:` followed by "\n" to stdout, where `` is the port actually bound (with `PORT=0`, the port the OS picked). This line is the only thing the server ever writes to stdout. 11 - Its data lives in the file named by the `DATA_FILE` environment variable, as JSON in a layout of your choice. An unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`. A relative `DATA_FILE`, the default included, is resolved against the current working directory, not the folder of `server.mjs`. 12 - The server reads the data file once, at startup. If reading it fails with `ENOENT` (the file, or a folder on its path, does not exist), there are no bookings yet. If reading it fails in any other way (for example the path is a directory), or its content is not data in the layout this server writes (for example it is empty or not valid JSON), the server writes `cannot read data file ` followed by "\n" to stderr, where `` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when it is unset or empty), and exits with code 1 without listening. 13 - After startup the server's memory is the truth: changes made to the file from outside are not noticed. The server writes the data file only when a POST creates a booking or a DELETE removes one, never at startup or for any other request, and it never creates folders. 14 - Every change is saved to the data file before its reply is sent: after a restart with the same `DATA_FILE`, the bookings, and the id the next booking will get, are as before. 15 - If saving a change fails (for example because the data file's folder does not exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included. Any other unexpected failure while handling a request also replies 500 `internal error`. In both cases the server keeps running. 16 - Requests that arrive at the same time give the same result as if they had been handled one at a time in some order: of several overlapping bookings sent at once while saving works, exactly one is created and every other one gets 409, and no id is given twice. 17 - Before sending any reply, the server reads the whole request body, if there is one, and discards what it does not use, so the client always receives the reply, the 413 and 415 replies included. 18 19 ## API 20 - The rooms are fixed: `Aurora`, `Borealis` and `Cosmos`, in that order. 21 - A booking is a JSON object with exactly the keys `id`, `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: `id` is a number, the others are strings. The first booking gets id 1 and each new booking the next integer; an id is never reused, even after deletes and restarts. 22 - Only the parsed JSON of a reply body matters: whitespace and key order in it are free. 23 - A request's path is its request target up to the first `?` (all of it when there is no `?`). Routes compare the path byte for byte, with no percent-decoding and no dot-segment, slash or letter-case normalisation: `/api/%62ookings`, `/api/./rooms`, `/API/rooms` and `/api/bookings/` are none of the paths below. The query, the text after the first `?`, is ignored unless stated, and is decoded as `new URLSearchParams(query)` does. 24 - `GET /api/rooms`: 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}`. 25 - `GET /api/bookings`: 200 `{"bookings": [...]}` with every booking, sorted by date, then start, then room in the order above. When the query has a `date` parameter (as `params.has('date')` says; `?date` with no `=` counts, with the empty value), its value is `params.get('date')` (the first one when repeated) and the reply holds only the bookings on that date; a value that is not a valid date by rule 6 below (the empty value included) gets 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. Other query parameters are ignored. 26 - `POST /api/bookings` with a JSON body holding `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`: 201 and the new booking. Other keys in the body are ignored. 27 - `DELETE /api/bookings/`: every path that is `/api/bookings/` followed by a non-empty `` holding no `/` is this route, whatever `` is. The reply is 204 with an empty body, and the booking is gone. When `` is not a positive integer written in ASCII digits 0-9 without a leading zero, or no booking has that id: 404 `booking not found`. 28 - `GET /` and `GET /app.js` serve the page (see Page). 29 - Any other path: 404 `not found`, whatever the method. This includes every path that starts with `/api/bookings/` and whose rest is empty or holds a `/`, such as `/api/bookings/` and `/api/bookings/1/`. 30 - A path above with a method not listed for it (HEAD and OPTIONS included): 405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/abc` is 405. A 405 reply may or may not have an `Allow` header; it is not checked. 31 - Every reply with a body other than the page and the script has `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`. An error reply is `{"error": ""}` with exactly that key, where `` is the text given here. 32 33 ## Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`; the first rule that fails decides the reply) 34 1. The media type of the `Content-Type` header (the part before the first `;`, with spaces and tabs removed from both ends, letter case ignored) is not `application/json`, or the header is missing: 415 `content type must be application/json`. 35 2. The body is longer than 10000 bytes, counting the body bytes actually received: 413 `body too large`. 36 3. The body, decoded as `Buffer.prototype.toString('utf8')` does and then given to `JSON.parse`, is not a JSON object (it is empty, not valid JSON, `null`, an array, a string, a number or a boolean): 400 `body must be a JSON object`. Bytes that are not valid UTF-8 become U+FFFD and are not an error by themselves. A byte order mark at the very start is kept, so such a body is not valid JSON. 37 4. `room` is not a string equal to one of the room names (letter case matters): 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos`. 38 5. `title` is not a string, or is shorter than 1 or longer than 80 UTF-16 code units after removing the whitespace at both ends (as `String.prototype.trim` does): 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters`. The booking keeps the trimmed title. 39 6. `date` is not a string `YYYY-MM-DD` (4, 2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) naming a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31, where February has 29 days in years divisible by 4: 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date`. 40 7. `start` is not a string `HH:MM` (2 and 2 ASCII digits 0-9) from `00:00` to `23:59`: 400 `start must be HH:MM`. 41 8. `end` is not such a string: 400 `end must be HH:MM`. 42 9. `end` is not later than `start`: 400 `end must be after start`. 43 10. The booking overlaps a booking of the same room on the same date, that is each of the two starts before the other ends (a booking may start exactly when another ends): 409 `room is already booked from to `, with the start and end of the overlapping booking that starts earliest. 44 - No field except `title` is trimmed or changed: ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and `9:00` are invalid. 45 46 ## Page 47 - `GET /` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/html; charset=utf-8` and the page. `GET /app.js` answers 200 with `Content-Type: text/javascript; charset=utf-8` and the page's script. 48 - The page loads the script with a `

6	- Saving: write to the data file (writeFile directly to the path; no folder creation). Serialize all mutations through one promise queue so concurrent POSTs behave sequentially. Apply in-memory change only after the write succeeded.

10	- 2026-11-03 · frontend · Book/Cancel re-enable runs in the request helper's `finally`, in the same tick fetch/json() settles, before the outcome is handled. Why: "enabled again as soon as the request settles, before anything else happens".
11	- 2026-11-03 · backend · Data file accepted only in the exact layout the server writes (exact keys, nextId > every id, unique ids, trimmed titles, no overlapping bookings); ENOTDIR (a file on the path) is not ENOENT, so it fails startup. Why: stricter reading of "not data in the layout this server writes" / "fails with ENOENT".
12	- 2026-11-03 · backend · Content-Type media type: ASCII-only lowercasing, trims only spaces/tabs (not String.trim). DELETE id compared as a string to stored ids, so huge ids never round onto an existing id. CONNECT is answered 404/405 on the raw socket. Why: stricter readings of rule 1, the delete id rule and "whatever the method".
13	- 2026-11-03 · testing · package.json test script is `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`: on Node 22 `node --test test/` treats `test/` as a module and fails. Why: `npm test` must run every test file.
14	- 2026-11-03 · testing · Near-miss copies (`.team/near-miss/<n>-<file>`, built by `.team/tools/near-miss-make.mjs`) are swapped in and restored inside a scratch copy of the project in the OS temp folder (`.team/tools/near-miss-run.mjs`), never in the real tree. Why: other sections edit server.mjs in parallel; an in-place swap could overwrite their edits.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. schema.name: Grep
schema.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

1	# Room bookings
2	
3	A small meeting-room booking app. It is one HTTP server, `server.mjs`, that:
4	
5	- serves a JSON API for listing, creating and cancelling bookings of three fixed rooms
6	  (`Aurora`, `Borealis`, `Cosmos`),
7	- serves a browser page (`public/index.html` and `public/app.js`) that uses that API,
8	- keeps every booking in one JSON data file.
9	
10	## Requirements
11	
12	- Node.js 22 or later.
13	- No dependencies: the server and the tests use Node.js built-ins only, so there is
14	  nothing to `npm install`.
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	Start the server with either command from the project folder:
19	
20	```sh
21	npm start
22	# or
23	node server.mjs
24	```
25	
26	When it is ready it prints one line to stdout:
27	
28	```
29	listening on http://127.0.0.1:3000
30	```
31	
32	The server only listens on `127.0.0.1` (this machine). That line is the only thing it
33	ever writes to stdout.
34	
35	### Configuration
36	
37	Both settings are environment variables.
38	
39	| Variable    | Default         | Meaning |
40	|-------------|-----------------|---------|
41	| `PORT`      | `3000`          | Port to listen on. Unset or empty means `3000`. Must be ASCII digits only and at most `65535`. `PORT=0` lets the OS pick a free port; the printed line shows the port actually bound. |
42	| `DATA_FILE` | `bookings.json` | Path of the JSON data file. Unset or empty means `bookings.json`. A relative path (the default included) is resolved against the **current working directory**, not the folder of `server.mjs`. |
43	
44	Examples:
45	
46	```sh
47	PORT=8080 npm start
48	DATA_FILE=/var/lib/rooms/bookings.json node server.mjs
49	PORT=0 DATA_FILE=tmp/test.json node server.mjs
50	```
51	
52	### Startup order and errors
53	
54	At startup the server checks `PORT`, then reads the data file, then starts listening.
55	If any step fails it writes one line to stderr and exits with code 1 without serving:
56	
57	| Problem | stderr line |
58	|---------|-------------|
59	| `PORT` is not only digits, or is above 65535 | `invalid PORT "<value>"` |
60	| The data file cannot be read (other than "does not exist"), or its content is not in the layout this server writes (empty, not valid JSON, wrong shape) | `cannot read data file <name>` |
61	| The port cannot be bound (for example it is already in use) | `cannot listen on port <port>: <error code>` |
62	
63	`<name>` is the value of `DATA_FILE` as given (`bookings.json` when unset or empty).
64	A data file that does not exist, or whose folder does not exist, is not an error: the
65	server simply starts with no bookings.
66	
67	## Using the page
68	
69	With the server running, open <http://127.0.0.1:3000> in a browser (use your `PORT` if
70	you changed it). The page lets you:
71	
72	- book a room: pick the room, enter a title, date, start and end, then press **Book**;
73	- see the bookings, one per line as `<date> <start>-<end> <room>: <title>`;
74	- show only one day's bookings with **Show date**, or every booking with **Show all**;
75	- cancel a booking with its **Cancel** button.
76	
77	The page does not check the fields itself; any error the server returns (for example
78	`room is already booked from 09:00 to 10:00`) is shown above the list. If the server
79	cannot be reached the page shows `Could not reach the server.`
80	
81	## API
82	
83	All API replies with a body are JSON with `Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`.
84	Errors are `{"error": "<message>"}`.
85	
86	A booking looks like this:
87	
88	```json
89	{ "id": 1, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
90	```
91	
92	Ids start at 1 and increase by one per new booking. An id is never reused, even after
93	deletes and restarts.
94	
95	### Routes
96	
97	| Method and path | Success | Errors |
98	|-----------------|---------|--------|
99	| `GET /api/rooms` | 200 `{"rooms": ["Aurora", "Borealis", "Cosmos"]}` | |
100	| `GET /api/bookings` | 200 `{"bookings": [...]}`, sorted by date, then start, then room (in the order above) | |
101	| `GET /api/bookings?date=YYYY-MM-DD` | 200, only that day's bookings | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
102	| `POST /api/bookings` | 201 and the new booking | see booking rules below |
103	| `DELETE /api/bookings/<id>` | 204, empty body | 404 `booking not found` |
104	| `GET /` | 200, the page (`text/html; charset=utf-8`) | |
105	| `GET /app.js` | 200, the page script (`text/javascript; charset=utf-8`) | |
106	
107	Other replies, for every route:
108	
109	- Any other path, whatever the method: 404 `not found`. Paths are compared exactly as
110	  sent (no decoding or case folding), so `/API/rooms`, `/api/bookings/` and
111	  `/api/bookings/1/` are all 404.
112	- A known path with a method it does not support (including `HEAD` and `OPTIONS`):
113	  405 `method not allowed`. For example `GET /api/bookings/1` is 405.
114	- An unexpected failure, including a failed save of the data file: 500 `internal error`.
115	  Nothing changes and the server keeps running.
116	
117	Notes:
118	
119	- The query string is ignored except for `date` on `GET /api/bookings`. `?date` with no
120	  value counts as an empty (invalid) date; when `date` is repeated, the first one is used.
121	- `DELETE` returns 404 `booking not found` both when no booking has that id and when
122	  `<id>` is not a positive whole number without a leading zero (for example `abc` or `01`).
123	
124	### Example
125	
126	```sh
127	curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings \
128	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
129	  -d '{"room":"Aurora","title":"Standup","date":"2026-11-03","start":"09:00","end":"10:00"}'
130	
131	curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings?date=2026-11-03'
132	
133	curl -s -X DELETE http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/bookings/1 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n'
134	```
135	
136	### Booking rules (`POST /api/bookings`)
137	
138	The body must be a JSON object with `room`, `title`, `date`, `start` and `end`; other keys
139	are ignored. Rules are checked in this order and the first failure decides the reply:
140	
141	| # | Rule | Reply on failure |
142	|---|------|------------------|
143	| 1 | `Content-Type` media type is `application/json` (case-insensitive, parameters such as `charset` allowed) | 415 `content type must be application/json` |
144	| 2 | Body is at most 10000 bytes | 413 `body too large` |
145	| 3 | Body is a JSON object (not empty, `null`, an array or another value) | 400 `body must be a JSON object` |
146	| 4 | `room` is exactly `Aurora`, `Borealis` or `Cosmos` (case matters) | 400 `room must be one of Aurora, Borealis, Cosmos` |
147	| 5 | `title` is a string of 1 to 80 characters after trimming whitespace at both ends; the trimmed title is stored | 400 `title must be 1 to 80 characters` |
148	| 6 | `date` is `YYYY-MM-DD`, a real day from 2000-01-01 to 2099-12-31 | 400 `date must be a valid YYYY-MM-DD date` |
149	| 7 | `start` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `start must be HH:MM` |
150	| 8 | `end` is `HH:MM` from `00:00` to `23:59` | 400 `end must be HH:MM` |
151	| 9 | `end` is later than `start` | 400 `end must be after start` |
152	| 10 | No overlap with another booking of the same room on the same date (back-to-back is fine) | 409 `room is already booked from <start> to <end>` (the earliest-starting overlapping booking) |
153	
154	Only `title` is trimmed; other fields must be exact, so ` 2026-11-03`, `2026-11-3` and
155	`9:00` are rejected.
156	
157	Requests sent at the same time are handled as if one after the other: of several
158	overlapping bookings sent at once, exactly one is created and the others get 409, and
159	no id is given twice.
160	
161	## Data file
162	
163	The data file is JSON in this layout:
164	
165	```json
166	{
167	  "nextId": 3,
168	  "bookings": [
169	    { "id": 2, "room": "Aurora", "title": "Standup", "date": "2026-11-03", "start": "09:00", "end": "10:00" }
170	  ]
171	}
172	```
173	
174	`nextId` is the id the next booking will get. The server writes the file compactly (one
175	line); the layout above is spread out only for reading.
176	
177	Persistence behaviour:
178	
179	- The file is read once, at startup. After that the server's memory is the truth; edits
180	  made to the file while the server runs are not noticed (and are overwritten by the
181	  next save).
182	- The file is written only when a `POST` creates a booking or a `DELETE` removes one,
183	  never at startup or for any other request.
184	- Each change is saved before its reply is sent, so after a restart with the same
185	  `DATA_FILE` the bookings and the next id are as before.
186	- The server never creates folders. If a save fails (for example the folder does not
187	  exist), the reply is 500 `internal error` and nothing changes, the next id included.
188	- At startup the file must be exactly in the layout the server writes (exact keys,
189	  valid fields, unique ids below `nextId`, no overlapping bookings); otherwise the
190	  server exits with `cannot read data file <name>`.
191	
192	## Tests
193	
194	```sh
195	npm test
196	```
197	
198	This runs `node --test test/`, using Node's built-in test runner (`node:test`). Nothing
199	needs to be installed.
200	
201	## Project layout
202	
203	```
204	server.mjs          HTTP server: API, page serving, data file load and save
205	public/index.html   the booking page
206	public/app.js       the page's script (classic script, no build step)
207	test/               node:test tests
208	test/helpers/       test helpers (fake-dom.mjs: a minimal DOM to run app.js under Node)
209	package.json        "start" and "test" scripts; no dependencies
210	README.md           this file
211	```
212

content.text: I can't run ad-hoc probes, so I'll check that the startup tests cover these scenarios instead.

I found no spec violations in the code. One required fix is in the README: it states the wrong test command. The verdict is a pass.

`npm test` gave 414 passing out of 414. I couldn't run my own probes, because Bash only allows the test command here. So I checked startup failures by reading the code and confirming the tests in `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/test/startup.test.mjs` cover them: bad PORT values, port in use, a data path that is a directory, a file in the middle of the path, and a byte order mark (BOM) at the start of the file.

## (A) Must fix

1. **README gives the wrong test command.** `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/README.md:198` says `This runs node --test test/`. The script in `package.json` is `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`. Per the decisions file, `node --test test/` fails on Node 22, so anyone following the README gets a failing run.

### Spec lines checked against the code, all as specified
- **Startup:** PORT is checked first, then the data file is read, then the server listens. PORT must be ASCII digits only and at most 65535, using a regex with no multiline flag, so trailing newlines and Arabic-Indic digits are rejected. An unset or empty PORT means 3000. If the port can't be bound, the server writes one line and exits 1. The PORT error line runs the value through `JSON.stringify`, so a PORT containing a newline still gives one line. stdout gets only the `listening on` line, with the port actually bound.
- **Data file:** an unset or empty `DATA_FILE` means `bookings.json`, and relative paths resolve against the current working directory. ENOENT means no bookings yet. Any other read error, or content not in the exact written layout, gives `cannot read data file <name as given>`. The file is written only on a successful POST or DELETE, and memory changes only after the write succeeds (lines 159-163). All changes go through one queue, so overlapping bookings sent at once give exactly one 201 and the rest 409.
- **Request body:** the whole body is read before any reply (line 293), so 413 and 415 replies arrive. The content type is checked before the size. The size counts the bytes actually received. A BOM is kept, because `Buffer#toString` does not strip it.
- **Routing:** paths are compared raw. `/api/bookings/<id>` matches only when the id is non-empty and has no `/`. The DELETE id must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$` and is compared as a string. HEAD, OPTIONS and CONNECT get 405 or 404. The `?date` filter uses `has`/`get`. The 204 reply has no body.
- **Booking rules 1-10:** they run in order. The title uses `trim` and is limited by UTF-16 length. Date and time checks use ASCII digits with leap years every 4 years. The overlap check uses strict `<` on both sides, and the 409 names the overlapping booking that starts earliest.
- **Page:** the script is the last element in `<body>`, with no `type`, `defer` or `async`. There are no inline scripts, no `<option>` elements, no room names and no `http(s)://`. The script uses only the allowed APIs. Book and Cancel are re-enabled in the request helper's `finally`. Only the last list fetch started is used. A 204 skips `json()`. On 201 only the title is cleared. Show all fetches once without dispatching an event.

## (B) Optional findings
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:161` writes the file directly with `writeFile`. If a write half-fails (for example the disk is full), the file can be left truncated: memory says nothing changed, but the next startup exits with `cannot read data file`. Writing to a temporary file in the same folder and then renaming it would avoid this; it creates no folders.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:317-321`: `handleConnect` builds the JSON error body separately from `sendJson`/`sendError`. A small shared `errorBody(message)` helper would remove that duplication.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:279-287`: `dispatch` chooses what to do by comparing `route.name` strings. Putting a handler function on each route returned by `matchRoute` would be more cohesive.
- `/root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/.team/notes/decisions.md:4` still lists the old test script, which line 13 later replaces. It's a notes file, not shipped code.

## GRADE
Overall: 9/10
Verdict: pass
structure: 9 — small single-purpose functions, frozen immutable store, changes go through one queue; dispatch chooses by string name
naming: 9 — names are clear and consistent (MSG, matchRoute, findEarliestOverlap, latestListRequest)
duplication: 9 — the CONNECT error body repeats sendJson's serialisation
size: 10 — server.mjs 363 lines, app.js 201, every function well under 50 lines
errors: 9 — friendly one-line startup failures, codes kept apart (ENOENT vs others), 500 without crashing, no swallowed errors; the direct writeFile can leave a truncated file on a partial failure
tests: n/a — written and graded by the testing section (414 pass)
security: 9 — no secrets, no HTML injection (only textContent and append), body size counted, input validated at the boundary
leftovers: 10 — no console.log, no commented-out code, no TODOs
Fixes:
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/README.md:198 change "This runs `node --test test/`" to "This runs `node --test "test/**/*.test.mjs"`" to match package.json
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:161 (optional) write to a temp file in the same folder and rename it over the data file, so a partial write can't leave a file the next startup rejects
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:317 (optional) share the `{error}` JSON body builder with sendError
- /root/bench-runs/h4-ec2b7dbc/server.mjs:279 (optional) have matchRoute return a handler function instead of a name that dispatch compares as a string
